 The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice on a plea filed by Tina A. Ambani, wife of industrialist Anil Ambani, seeking disclosure of whether any Look-Out Circular (LOC) has been issued against her by investigating agencies, including the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED).
 Justice Mini Pushkarna sought response of Bureau of Immigration, ED and SFIO while listing the matter on December 08. 
 Ambani has also sought suspension of any such LOC, if issued against her, to enable her to travel to Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bhutan between December 10 and December 30.
 She has sought directions to the Bureau of Immigration and the investigating agencies to disclose the existence and particulars of any LOC against her, including its copy, the originating agency, the case or proceeding in which it was opened, the date of issuance, reference number, grounds recorded and present status.
 Advocate Arshdeep Singh Khurana appearing for Ambani submitted that she wants to travel abroad to visit her family and friends and therefore, wants to know if any travel restrictions have been imposed against her.
 He said that though the two agencies had summoned her, there are no pending summons as of now and that she has not been called any further. 
 “I wish to travel from December 10 to visit my family. This is a disclosure petition that if there is an LOC, they may tell me and if there is no LOC, then it may come on record,” he said.
 Appearing for ED, Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain said that two summons were issued to Ambani however she did not appear in response to either of them. 
 As he sought time to file a short response to the plea, Khurana told Court that Ambani had communicated to the agency her willingness to appear but was suffering from a spinal fracture at the relevant time. He said that after her intimation, no further summons have been issued to her. 
 The petition states that Ambani apprehends that an LOC may have been opened against her at the instance of the ED in connection with an ECIR of 2025 or by the SFIO in connection with its investigation into the affairs of certain Reliance Group companies.
 The SFIO is investigating the affairs of Reliance Home Finance Limited, Reliance Capital Limited, Reliance Infrastructure Limited and CLE Private Limited, as well as Reliance Communications Limited, Reliance Communications Infrastructure Limited and Reliance Infratel Limited.
 According to the petition, the SFIO issued a summons to Ambani on July 20, under Section 217 of the Companies Act, 2013, in her capacity as a director of Mandke Foundation and former director of Reliance Project Ventures and Management Private Limited, entities stated to have had transactions with the companies under investigation.
 She responded through her advocates on July 29 and subsequently, through a letter dated October 05, expressed her willingness to travel to New Delhi and appear before the SFIO on October 29 or 30. However, the agency neither fixed a date for her appearance nor issued any further summons, the petition states.
 Separately, the ED had issued two summons to her in February under Section 50 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), requiring her to appear on February 9 and 17. She submitted replies to the summons on February 16 and 20. No further summons or communication has been issued by the ED thereafter, the petition states.
 Ambani has stated that she is not named as an accused in any FIR, prosecution complaint or other criminal proceeding.
 The petition also refers to two earlier petitions filed by her sons, Jai Anshul A. Ambani and Jai Anmol A. Ambani , seeking disclosure of LOCs, if any, issued against them. The Court had disposed of the petitions on September 17 and October 12, respectively, after the authorities agreed to treat them as representations and communicate the requisite information within three and four weeks, respectively.
 The petition has been filed through advocates Neeha Nagpal, Vishvendra Tomar and Arjun Singh.
